article.articleHeadline: Dengue And Swine Flu Cases Surge In Mumbai, Here's How To Stay Safe During Monsoon
article.articleSummary: Dengue, leptospirosis and swine flu surge in Mumbai during the monsoon, driven by waterlogged streets and floodwaters. No exact case counts are provided, but authorities say cases are rising. The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has intensified prevention, conducting thousands of inspections and fogging more than 30 lakh homes to curb mosquito breeding. Dengue is transmitted by mosquitoes; leptospirosis exposure occurs from floodwater, especially with cuts; swine flu tends to spread in humid, crowded conditions. Residents are urged to seek medical care promptly, with guidance to consult a doctor within 24 to 72 hours after exposure or if fever, body aches or breathing problems appear. Preventive steps include wearing full-sleeve clothing, using mosquito repellent, avoiding stagnant water, and maintaining hygiene during the monsoon.

triage.headline_ja: ムンバイでデング熱と豚インフルエンザの症例が急増、モンスーン期の安全対策とは
triage.triage_reason: 毎年のモンスーン期に発生する季節性感染症（デング熱、レプトスピラ症、豚インフルエンザ）の増加であり、具体的な症例数や異常性の情報がなく、通常の公衆衛生対応の範囲内と見られる。
triage.notes: モンスーン期に毎年見られる季節性感染症の増加を報じる一般的な健康啓発記事。BMCが予防対策（防疫・啓発）を実施しており、地域内で管理可能と見られる。具体的な症例数や重症度、異常な増加傾向についての情報はない。

article.articleHeadline: 国家疾控局：全国新冠病毒疫情目前处于低流行水平
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: National CDC: The nationwide COVID-19 outbreak is currently at a low level of transmission.
article.articleSummary: On July 16, 2026, the National Center for Disease Control and Prevention (China CDC) held a briefing. Spokesperson Xi Jingjing said summer mosquito breeding is active, travel increases, raising risks of vector-borne disease and local transmission from imported cases; southern provinces face clustered dengue fever and chikungunya fever risks. Nationally, respiratory infections remain at a low level; rhinovirus and parainfluenza viruses show activity, while COVID-19 is currently at a low transmission level. The country is in a peak flood season described as 'Seven Up Eight Down' with widespread floods and associated environmental hygiene challenges, potentially impacting food and drinking water safety and altering dynamics of vector and reservoir animals, increasing risks of enteric, respiratory, and vector-borne diseases in affected areas. Source: Yangcheng Evening News, Yangcheng Pai, Jin Yang Wang.

triage.headline_ja: 国家疾病予防管理局：全国の新型コロナウイルス感染症流行は現在低い流行レベルにある
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19は低流行水準との通常の定期報告だが、夏季のデング熱・チクングニア熱のクラスターリスクや洪水による衛生課題への言及があり、今後の動向を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 本記事は中国疾病予防管理局の定例記者会見報告であり、COVID-19自体は低流行水準。デング熱・チクングニア熱の季節的リスクおよび洪水による衛生問題への言及があるが、具体的な症例数や地域名は不明。

article.articleHeadline: V Konžskej demokratickej republike zaznamenali viac ako dvetisíc prípadov eboly vrátane 754 úmrtí
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, more than 2,000 Ebola cases were recorded, including 754 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo has recorded over 2,000 Ebola cases and 754 deaths from the Bundibugyo ebolavirus variant. The World Health Organization cautions the true scope may be two to four times higher than official figures and notes the outbreak has spread to five provinces. There are no approved vaccines or therapies for Bundibugyo Ebola. On Tuesday, the first clinical trial evaluating the antiviral obeldesivir began for people who had contact with infected patients, under the EBO-PEP program. The experimental drug from Gilead Sciences showed potential against filoviruses in preclinical studies. Medecins Sans Frontieres warns the outbreak is spreading at an unprecedented rate, reaching new areas; in under five weeks, confirmed cases reportedly tripled and deaths more than quintupled. Many new patients die before seeking care. The trial aims to assess obeldesivir’s efficacy in exposed contacts.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国で2,000人以上のエボラ症例を記録、754人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱が5州に拡大し2,000例超・死亡754人、致死率が高く未承認治療薬のみという状況はIHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当し、国際的関心も高い。
triage.notes: WHOは公式統計の2〜4倍の実数を懸念しており、MSFも前例のない速度での拡大を報告。承認済みワクチン・治療薬が存在しないブンディブギョ株であることも重大性を高めている。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو الديمقراطية تعلن ارتفاع عدد الإصابات بفيروس إيبولا إلى 2073 - بوابة الشروق
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Democratic Republic of the Congo announces that the number of Ebola virus infections has risen to 2,073 - Shorouk Portal
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 2,073 confirmed cases and 796 deaths as of July 14, 2026. The World Health Organization estimates the true number of infections is at least two to four times higher. The outbreak, the seventeenth Ebola outbreak in the DRC, is driven by the Bundibugyo virus strain, for which there is no vaccine or treatment. Most fatalities occurred at home rather than in health facilities, while health workers have threatened to strike over unpaid salaries. The May 15 declaration marked the start of this wave. International partners and African nations have mobilized about $1.5 billion to bolster the response and strengthen medical infrastructure. WHO Emergency Programme Chief Chikwe Ihekweazu spoke after visiting the region, underscoring the scale of transmission and the need for sustained action.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラウイルス感染者数が2,073人に増加と発表 - Shorouk Portal
triage.triage_reason: 大規模なエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク（2,073症例、796死亡）でワクチン・治療法のないブンディブギョ株が原因であり、国際的関心・支援も高く、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: ワクチン・治療法のないブンディブギョ株による第17次エボラ流行。医療従事者の未払い賃金によるストライキの脅威、家庭内での死亡が多い点も懸念材料。国際的に15億ドルの支援が動員されている。

article.articleHeadline: الصحة العالمية تشكك في أرقام إصابات إيبولا المعلنة في الكونغو
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization casts doubt on the announced Ebola case numbers in the Congo.
article.articleSummary: World Health Organization casts doubt on official Ebola case counts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, estimating true infections may be 2–4 times higher. As of July 16, 2026, at least 1,963 cases and 719 deaths have been reported, with most fatalities occurring at home rather than in clinics. The current outbreak, in Ituri province, is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there is no licensed vaccine or approved treatment. The Rwampara Ebola Treatment Center in Ituri has 384 confirmed infections and 89 deaths. Healthcare workers account for a large share of cases, including 112 transmissions and 35 deaths, amid threats of a full strike after two months without pay. The government acknowledges payroll delays and is attempting corrections. The outbreak began around May 15, marking the seventeenth Ebola outbreak, with international partners mobilizing about $1.5 billion to support the response and health infrastructure.

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機関、コンゴにおける発表されたエボラ感染者数に疑問を呈する
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準2つ以上（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常事態）に該当し、WPRO基準も複数該当（重症度高、ワクチン未承認、医療従事者感染拡大、国際支援必要）。DRCで進行中の大規模エボラアウトブレイクでありフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: WHOが公式の感染者数の正確性に疑問を呈しており、実際の感染者数は報告の2〜4倍の可能性があると指摘。医療従事者への給与未払いによるストライキの脅威も、対応能力に影響を与える懸念材料。ワクチン・治療薬未承認のBundibugyoエボラウイルスによる第17次アウトブレイクであり、国際社会が約15億ドルを動員して対応中。

article.articleHeadline: El ébola se propaga sin precedentes dos meses después de la declaración de la epidemia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola spreads at an unprecedented rate two months after the epidemic was declared.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (Ituri province) spreading at an unprecedented rate two months after declaration. As of July 13, over 2,000 cases and more than 750 deaths. Ituri accounts for about 90% of confirmed cases; outbreak declared May 15; WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 17. The crisis unfolds amid armed conflict and displacement, with weak access to care, overwhelmed surveillance, and strained treatment centers; MSF urges more resources for community engagement, surveillance, diagnostics, and patient care. The outbreak has crossed into Uganda, reporting 20 confirmed infections (15 imported from the Congo) and two deaths. The circulating strain is Bundibugyo, with a 30–50% fatality rate; no approved vaccine or specific treatment. Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids; symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and hemorrhagic manifestations. Upcoming rainy season could raise malaria burden and further strain health systems.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱、流行宣言から2カ月後に前例のない速さで拡大
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEICを宣言済みのエボラ流行で、2000人超の感染・750人超の死亡、ウガンダへの越境拡大も確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大な公衆衛生危機である。
triage.notes: ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。記事はWHOが既にPHEICを宣言済みの進行中のエボラ流行を扱っており、マラリア流行期の到来による医療システムへの更なる負荷も懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Ébola: Uganda Prepara-se Para Declarar Fim do Surto
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Uganda prepares to declare the end of the outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Uganda is set to discharge its last Ebola patient on Thursday, 16 July, starting a 42-day countdown required by the World Health Organization to declare the country Ebola-free. Government spokesperson Alan Kasujja said the patient’s discharge from Mulago National Referral Hospital in Kampala would initiate the surveillance period. The broader outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), which the WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in May, has recorded 2,011 confirmed cases and 754 confirmed deaths as of 15 July, per government data cited by Reuters. In Uganda, the Health Ministry portal on 16 July lists 17 recoveries, one patient in isolation, and two deaths, with five locally acquired and 15 imported cases. All Ugandan cases are linked to Bundibugyo ebolavirus, the WHO noting it as the third-largest outbreak caused by this strain; if 42 days pass without new cases, Uganda would be declared Ebola-free under WHO guidelines.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ:ウガンダ、流行終息宣言の準備を進める
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEICを宣言した進行中のエボラ流行（DRC・ウガンダ）に関する続報であり、深刻な公衆衛生上の影響と国際的拡大が確認されているためフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はウガンダにおける流行終息への動きだが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため、DRCのみをverified_locationsに含めた。DRCでの流行は2026年5月にWHOがPHEICを宣言した大規模流行の一部であり、引き続き監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: صحيفة عمون : أمريكا تمنع مواطنيها المقيمين في الكونجو من العودة الفورية بسبب إيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The United States bars its citizens living in Congo from returning immediately due to Ebola.
article.articleSummary: On 16 July 2026, the United States imposed travel restrictions linked to the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, barring U.S. citizens and dual nationals who were in the DRC within the previous 21 days from entering the United States on commercial flights. The U.S. embassy in Kinshasa states that travelers who were in the DRC during the 21 days before their trip will not be allowed to board US-bound commercial flights, and all U.S. citizens and dual nationals who were in the DRC should plan to remain outside the United States for 21 days before entry. The measures come as Ebola has spread to several provinces within the DRC. Dr. Daniel Jernigan, a CDC official who led the 2014-2015 West Africa Ebola response, said using a 'no-boarding' policy to bring citizens home when risk is low is unprecedented. Reuters had reported earlier on the policy.

triage.headline_ja: オンマンニュース：米国、コンゴ在住の自国民のエボラによる即時帰国を禁止
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラが複数州に拡大し、米国が異例の渡航制限（no-boarding policy）を課すなど国際的な対応が生じており、IHR基準を複数満たすためフルRRAへ進むべき事案。
triage.notes: 米国および周辺国（アンゴラ等）は渡航制限措置の対象・関連地域として記載されているが、感染発生地としてはDRCのみが主題であるため、verified_locationsにはDRCのみを含めた。CDC元当局者が本措置を『前例のない』と評価している点も異常性を裏付ける。

article.articleHeadline: Haryana detects over 25,600 new TB cases
article.articleSummary: Haryana, India reports 25,666 new tuberculosis (TB) cases detected through the AI-driven 100-Day TB Mukt Bharat Campaign (Phase-II), launched March 24, 2026 (World TB Day). From March 24 to July 5, 2026, active case finding identified patients who might not seek care, with 3,914 health camps—2,854 in identified high-risk villages and urban wards. The drive relies on AI-enabled handheld X-ray machines for rapid screening in remote areas and the CATB (Cough Against TB) mobile app, which analyzes cough sounds to flag individuals for further testing. Vulnerability Mapping (VM-TB) pinpointed 2,111 high-risk locations to target screening. Led by Additional Chief Secretary Dr Sumita Misra, the campaign aims to enable early diagnosis and timely treatment to curb TB transmission in Haryana.

triage.headline_ja: ハリヤナ州で新たに25,600件以上の結核症例を検出
triage.triage_reason: 既知の風土病である結核の積極的スクリーニングキャンペーンの成果報告であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: AIを活用した結核撲滅キャンペーン（100-Day TB Mukt Bharat Campaign）による積極的症例発見の結果報告であり、新規アウトブレイクではない。

article.articleHeadline: ارتفاع عدد الإصابات بـ إيبولا في الكونغو إلى 2073 حالة - أردو بوینت
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola infections in Congo rise to 2,073 cases
article.articleSummary: Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, confirms Ebola virus infections have reached 2,073 with 796 deaths as of July 14, 2026. Reported July 16, 2026, the update provides no further breakdown on laboratory confirmation, infection sources, or imported/exported cases. This ongoing outbreak in the DRC shows a substantial fatality burden, with provisional figures indicating continued transmission through mid-July. The data emphasize the public health challenge posed by Ebola in the DRC and the need for sustained surveillance, patient management, and response measures. All figures are provisional and reflect cases through July 14.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ感染者数、2,073例に増加
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCで2,073例・796人死亡と大規模継続的アウトブレイクを示しており、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクがあるため。
triage.notes: 致死率約38%と高く、継続的な感染拡大が示唆される。詳細な感染源や検査確定情報は不明。

article.articleHeadline: Kabar Buruk untuk Warga Sumsel, DBD Tembus 2.149 Kasus di Bulan Juli 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bad News for South Sumatra Residents as Dengue Fever Cases Reach 2,149 in July 2026
article.articleSummary: 2,149 dengue fever cases reported in South Sumatra as of 14 July 2026 across 17 districts/cities, with Palembang City the epicenter at 619 cases. Other high counts include Muara Enim (440), Ogan Ilir (185), Lubuk Linggau (139), Banyuasin (129), Lahat (128), and OKU Timur (118). Total deaths reach 15, with Lahat recording the highest toll (4), followed by Lubuk Linggau (2); Musi Banyuasin, Banyuasin, Ogan Ilir, Palembang, PALI, and Musi Rawas Utara each reporting one fatality. No fatalities reported in OKU, OKI, Muara Enim, Musi Rawas, OKU Selatan, OKU Timur, Prabumulih, or Empat Lawang. The outbreak is being monitored by the regional health authorities. Authorities warn that El Niño could intensify from July–September 2026, raising temperatures and accelerating the Aedes mosquito lifecycle, potentially heightening transmission of dengue, chikungunya, and malaria.

triage.headline_ja: 南スマトラ住民に悪いニュース、2026年7月のデング熱症例が2,149件に到達
triage.triage_reason: インドネシア南スマトラで季節性のデング熱流行が報告されているが、同国では毎年発生する風土病であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低い。エルニーニョによる悪化懸念があり経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: デング熱はインドネシアで季節的に流行する風土病。死亡15例を含む2,149例が報告されているが、地域保健当局による監視下にあり、国際的な緊急性は低い。エルニーニョによる媒介蚊活動の活発化で今後の悪化が懸念されるため、続報を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: "إيبولا" يعود بقوة.. والعلم يردّ بأول لقاح واعد يواجه السلالة الأكثر فتكاً
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola makes a strong comeback... Science responds with the first promising vaccine to confront the deadliest strain.
article.articleSummary: Ebola Bundibugyo strain outbreak persists in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. Oxford University begins the first-in-human Phase I trial of an Ebola vaccine targeting Bundibugyo, enrolling 50 adults aged 18–55 to assess safety and immunogenicity. As of July 11, 2026, the DRC reports 1,926 cases and 702 deaths, while Uganda reports 20 cases. CEPI hails the trial as a step toward a safe, effective vaccine; Africa CDC notes that clinical trials are essential for future response tools, though not an immediate solution. Ugandan researchers plan additional trials after regulatory approvals as part of an international effort to develop three vaccines against the circulating strain. The outbreak now spans ten high-risk provinces including Kinshasa, underscoring urgent demand for scientific countermeasures.

triage.headline_ja: 「エボラ」が猛威を再び…科学は最も致死性の高い株に立ち向かう初の有望ワクチンで応戦
triage.triage_reason: DRCで1,926症例・702死亡、ウガンダにも拡大し10州に及ぶエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）の大規模アウトブレイクであり、IHR基準複数該当かつ国際的関心・支援ニーズも高い。
triage.notes: ウガンダでも20症例確認され国際的拡大が進行中だが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。CEPI主導のワクチン第I相試験が開始されており、国際支援体制が既に稼働している状況。

article.articleHeadline: COVID di China Naik Lagi Tembus 79 Ribu Kasus, Dipicu Varian Ini
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19 in China Rises Again, Surpasses 79,000 Cases, Driven by This Variant
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 in China surged in June 2026, with 79,000 laboratory-confirmed cases reported by the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention (China CDC). The tally includes 130 severe cases and 1 COVID-19–related death. Compared with May’s ~21,861 cases and April’s ~23,477, the June figure reflects a continuing rise in transmission. All June infections are attributed to the Omicron variant, and health authorities say there is no evidence of a new SARS-CoV-2 variant emerging. The report, cited by China Daily, notes the current upward trajectory of COVID-19 cases in China despite the absence of a detected novel strain. The release underscores ongoing monitoring and laboratory confirmation by national public health authorities as the country tracks the scale of the resurgence and its clinical severity.

triage.headline_ja: 中国のCOVID-19感染者数が再び増加、7万9千人を突破 この変異株が原因
triage.triage_reason: 既知のオミクロン変異株による季節性の感染再増加であり、新規変異株の出現や重症化率の異常な上昇は確認されていないため、通常のサーベイランス範囲内と判断される。
triage.notes: 79,000症例中、重症130例・死亡1例と重症化率は低く、既存のオミクロン株による季節的な増加と説明されている。新規変異株の証拠はなしと当局が明言しており、通常のサーベイランス報告に留まる。

article.articleHeadline: Uganda set to discharge last Ebola patient as WHO countdown begins
article.articleSummary: Uganda is poised to discharge its final Ebola patient at Mulago National Referral Hospital in Kampala, triggering a 42-day countdown under WHO rules to declare Ebola-free. Government spokesperson Alan Kasujja said the discharge will begin the countdown after which no new cases in 42 days would meet the standard. Uganda's health portal reports 17 recoveries, 1 patient in isolation, and 2 deaths, with 5 locally acquired and 15 imported cases, all linked to the Bundibugyo strain, described by WHO as the third-worst Ebola outbreak. In parallel, the Democratic Republic of Congo continues a major outbreak, with 2,011 confirmed cases and 754 deaths as of Wednesday; Ituri province is the epicentre and cross-border spread into Uganda has occurred. The outbreak was declared a public health emergency of international concern.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダ、WHOのカウントダウン開始とともに最後のエボラ患者を退院させる予定
triage.triage_reason: DRCで2,011例・754人死亡の大規模エボラ流行が継続しPHEIC宣言下にあり、ウガンダへの越境感染も発生していることから、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事の主眼はウガンダの流行終息だが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCでの継続的な大規模流行（PHEIC宣言、越境感染含む）が記事内で詳述されているため、DRCを検証済み発生地域として計上した。

article.articleHeadline: Video | NDTV Lifeline | Why Dengue Is No Longer Just a Monsoon Disease
article.articleSummary: Dengue in India is now reported beyond the monsoon season, a shift linked to climate change—rising temperatures, erratic rainfall, and changing weather patterns that alter disease spread. The NDTV Lifeline episode 'Why Dengue Is No Longer Just a Monsoon Disease' investigates how dengue reports extend beyond the monsoon and whether influenza seasons are becoming less predictable. It explains climate-driven disease dynamics and offers practical steps for individuals, communities, and health systems to stay protected. The discussion centers on India and highlights broader public health implications of warming climates on infectious disease transmission. The program airs on NDTV Profit: Saturdays at 7:30 PM and Sundays at 1:30 PM, with host Ambika Singh Kahma guiding the segment. Published 2026-07-16.

triage.triage_reason: 特定の急性アウトブレイクではなく、気候変動とデング熱・季節性インフルエンザの関連性を解説する報道番組であり、緊急のシグナルとは言えない。

article.articleHeadline: Profissionais da Vigilância em Saúde de Três Passos participam de capacitação sobre raiva e febre amarela - Três Passos News
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Public Health Surveillance professionals from Três Passos participate in training on rabies and yellow fever - Três Passos News
article.articleSummary: On July 14, 2026, Public Health Surveillance teams in Três Passos, Brazil, participated in a theoretical-practical training on the State Rabies Control and Prophylaxis Program and Yellow Fever Surveillance. Held at the Instituto Federal Farroupilha, Frederico Westphalen campus, the session was promoted by the 2nd Regional Health Coordination of Frederico Westphalen and covered Três Passos. Participants included nurses in Environmental Surveillance and Immunizations, an epidemiological surveillance nursing technician, and vector control agents. The program addressed the Rio Grande do Sul Rabies Control and Prophylaxis Program, laboratory diagnosis of rabies, human rabies prophylaxis, surveillance of pathogens in wild animals, yellow fever surveillance, scorpion surveillance, case studies, and sample collection practices. Coordinators emphasized that such capacity-building strengthens rapid, efficient responses to suspected diseases, enhancing surveillance, prevention, and protection of public health in the municipality.

article.articleHeadline: Mumbai Dengue Cases Up 28%, Malaria Up 18%, H1N1 Nearly Triples in 2026
article.articleSummary: In Mumbai, dengue cases have risen 28%, malaria 18%, and H1N1 nearly tripled in 2026, as heavy rainfall and widespread waterlogging sustain transmission. Leptospirosis risk rises from floodwaters contaminated with animal urine; residents are advised to take preventive medication if exposed, avoid walking barefoot, and wear protective footwear. The BMC has intensified surveillance, including a drive at nearly 3,000 construction sites screening 54,763 workers, with 37 laboratory-confirmed malaria cases treated. Vector-control teams are conducting large-scale anti-mosquito operations. Public guidance urges eliminating stagnant water, using repellents and nets, and seeking medical evaluation for fever, body aches, or persistent flu-like illness. Dr. Chhaya Vaja reports a 20% rise in viral infections among adults 22–65 over the past two months, with 2–3 of every 10 outpatients presenting fever-related complaints.

article.articleHeadline: 6月新冠新增7.9万例 国家疾控局：新冠疫情已演变为常见的呼吸道传染病，大家不用过度紧张__新快网
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In June, 79,000 new COVID-19 cases; National Center for Disease Control and Prevention says the COVID-19 outbreak has evolved into a common respiratory infectious disease, and there is no need to overreact.
article.articleSummary: June 2026 in China recorded 79,000 newly diagnosed COVID-19 cases across 31 provinces and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, with 130 severe cases and 1 death (involving underlying conditions). At a July 16 press briefing, China CDC stated that overall respiratory infections are at a low level, and COVID-19 is currently at a low-endemic level. An uptick occurred in late May, but by mid-June the situation returned to low levels; sentinel hospital SARS-CoV-2 positivity rates have risen slightly, indicating a mild upward trend rather than a surge. The dominant circulating lineage remains NB.1.8.1 series variants, with no new variant detected posing additional public health risk. Since October 2025, virus activity has persisted at an endemic/inter-epidemic level for about eight and a half months. Given summer travel, maintain hygiene, ventilation, and cough etiquette; seek medical care for fever or respiratory symptoms and follow medical advice.

article.articleHeadline: Уганда изписва последния пациент с ебола, започва 42-дневно обратно броене
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Uganda discharges the last Ebola patient as a 42-day countdown begins.
article.articleSummary: Uganda discharges its last Ebola patient, initiating a 42-day countdown to an official Ebola-free status under WHO guidelines (42 consecutive days without a new case after the last patient tests negative and is discharged). The Ugandan Ministry of Health reports 17 recoveries, one patient still in isolation, and two deaths. Of the total cases, five were domestically acquired and 15 imported. The final patient is set to be released from Mulago National Referral Hospital in Kampala on Thursday, after which the countdown begins. Concurrently, the Democratic Republic of Congo sustains a larger outbreak, with 2,011 confirmed cases and 754 deaths as of Wednesday, all linked to Bundibugyo ebolavirus—the third-largest outbreak of this strain to date, for which WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in May.

article.articleHeadline: Climate crisis threatens Asia's fight to eliminate tuberculosis
article.articleSummary: Climate crisis threatens TB elimination in Asia, with Indonesia among the hardest-hit. In 2024, TB infected at least 10.7 million people and caused 1.23 million deaths worldwide; Asia houses most cases, with Indonesia accounting for about 10% and India ~25%. Overcrowding, poor ventilation, food insecurity and malnutrition worsen transmission and disrupt care during extreme weather. Dense urban settings, such as Mumbai, risk higher transmission as reliance on air conditioning reduces ventilation. Pakistan’s floods disrupted TB services, prompting courier delivery of medicines and diagnostics. Experts urge single-visit testing for TB and comorbidities, active case finding and latent TB identification. Indonesia detected about 885,000 of an estimated 1 million annual cases in 2024; roughly 150,000 undiagnosed. Indonesia aims for 65 per 100,000 by 2030, shifting to identify undiagnosed cases via mass screening in 13 Central/West Java municipalities starting July 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Uganda to discharge last Ebola patient, spokesperson says
article.articleSummary: Uganda is set to discharge its last Ebola patient on Thursday from Mulago National Referral Hospital isolation unit, starting a 42-day countdown toward an Ebola-free declaration if no new cases emerge. The broader outbreak linked to the Bundibugyo strain is concentrated in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where the WHO declared a public health emergency in May. As of 2026-07-16, the DRC reports 2,011 confirmed cases and 754 confirmed deaths. In Uganda’s official portal, recoveries stand at 17, one current admission in isolation, and two deaths; five cases are locally acquired and 15 imported. All cases are linked to Bundibugyo. If the 42-day period passes without new infections, Uganda may be declared Ebola-free per WHO guidelines.

article.articleHeadline: 中國新冠病毒感染確診激增7.9萬! 青年教授高管接連病亡 官方數據遭質疑
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: China's COVID-19 confirmed infections surge by 79,000! Young professors and executives die in succession; official data under scrutiny.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 infections surge in Mainland China, with 79,000 new cases in June 2026 and 130 severe cases, per the China CDC. Sentinel hospital data show influenza-like illness COVID-19 positivity rising from 2.9% in early June to 6.4% in the final week, indicating ongoing community transmission. We also see reports of herpangina and hand-foot-and-mouth disease, with rhinovirus activity noted regionally. Within roughly six weeks, more than ten mid‑career professors and corporate executives have died, including Sun Fanglin, 58, head of Tongji University Translational Medicine Institute (died July 10, 2026); 37-year-old Liao Ke (independent director at Red Tower Securities); 54-year-old Sun Benhua (soil scientist); and 55-year-old Gao Shanwen (economist). Public skepticism about official data remains high amid concerns of underreporting. Hong Kong and Macao are also experiencing rising cases and deaths during a summer resurgence, stressing regional public-health defenses.

article.articleHeadline: Congo-Kinshasa: Ebola - Insécurité et méfiance freinent la riposte
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo-Kinshasa: Ebola - Insecurity and Mistrust Hinder the Response.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) progresses amid insecurity and mistrust. More than 2,000 cases and 754 deaths have been recorded two months after the outbreak was declared, with confirmed cases doubling in the last five weeks. The Bundibugyo variant has no licensed vaccine available. In Ituri, eastern DRC, nearly 900,000 people are displaced by conflict, while access to some zones is blocked by armed groups such as the ADF, and artisanal mining drives population movements. Widespread distrust of the health system—already weak before Ebola—hampers response, with many patients dying before reaching treatment and 80% of new infections arising from unknown transmission chains. Stigma and late presentation underscore the need for rapid community engagement and stronger surveillance. MSF advocates immediate scale-up of interventions and resources.

article.articleHeadline: संभल जाओ UP वालों! फिर लौटा आया कोरोना, 32 वर्षीय महिला मिली कोरोना पॉजिटिव, अलर्ट मोड पर स्वास्थ्य विभाग
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Watch out, UP residents! COVID-19 has returned again; a 32-year-old woman has tested positive for COVID-19; health department on alert.
article.articleSummary: On 16 July 2026, Ballia district, Uttar Pradesh, reported its first COVID-19 case in a long lull. A 32-year-old woman from Adarsh Nagar Panchayat, Sahatwar, Ward No. 5, tested positive for SARS-CoV-2. The sample was collected on 11 July at Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences (SGPGIMS) in Lucknow and reported positive on 13 July. After confirmation, health authorities initiated contact tracing; four close contacts at her home were tested, all of whom returned negative. The patient is in home isolation and under medical supervision, with ongoing monitoring by the district surveillance team led by Dr. Abhishek Mishra. The health department urged vigilance and advised anyone with fever, cold, cough or other respiratory symptoms to seek medical evaluation. No additional cases were reported at this time.

article.articleHeadline: Was mayonnaise the villain? Three under treatment for food poisoning from Al Reem test positive for Shigella
article.articleSummary: Shigellosis linked to Al Reem Hotel in Katrikadavu, Kochi, where an outbreak on July 11–12 sickened about 50 people. Three of the patients tested positive for Shigella after samples from 15 initially admitted patients were analyzed, with the district medical officer confirming the result. Investigators believe mayonnaise used with kuzhimanthi was the likely infection source; those who did not consume mayonnaise reportedly avoided illness. Some hoteliers and traders claim the municipal drinking water supply could be the culprit, but this has not been officially confirmed. The hotel was closed following complaints; samples were collected for testing; police have registered a case and are progressing with the investigation. A large protest occurred in front of the hotel in response to the confirmed Shigella cases.

article.articleHeadline: Appels sur l'actualité - RDC : l'épidémie d'Ebola est-elle sous-estimée?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Calls on Current Events - DRC: Is the Ebola outbreak underestimated?
article.articleSummary: WHO warns two months into the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo that official tallies exceed 2,000 cases and 754 deaths, though health authorities warn the true number of infections could be two to four times higher. The discrepancy prompts questions about underreporting, surveillance reach, and challenges in containment. The piece highlights uncertainties around how widespread transmission is and the reasons containment remains difficult. In Bunia this week, the first clinical trial of post-exposure prophylaxis for Ebola has been launched, aiming to prevent progression after exposure and potentially alter outbreak dynamics if effective. The development signals a new tool in the response amid ongoing efforts to curb transmission.

triage.notes: WHOが症例数の過小評価を警告しており、実際の感染者数は公式発表の2〜4倍の可能性。Bunia市で曝露後予防のための臨床試験が開始されたことも報告されている。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو.. ارتفاع إصابات "إيبولا إلى 2073 حالة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo: Ebola infections rise to 2,073 cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) continues. As of July 14, 2026, confirmed infections reach 2,073 with 796 deaths per official figures; the Ministry of Information cites over 2,000 infections, including 2,011 confirmed cases and 754 deaths. The outbreak spans five provinces, with Ituri in the northeast as the epicenter, bordering Uganda and South Sudan; Uganda has also reported cases and fatalities. Transmission occurs via direct contact with infected individuals or body fluids, and there is no specific vaccine or targeted therapy for the Bundibugyo strain currently involved. Since early July, two antiviral therapies are in clinical trials. Separately, the United States restricts entry for citizens and residents who have been in the DRC within the previous 21 days, barring them from commercial flights and advising a 21-day stay outside the country before US entry.

article.articleHeadline: 國家疾控局：內地新冠病毒總體處於低流行水平 - 香港文匯報
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: National CDC: Mainland China Overall at a Low Level of COVID-19 Transmission
article.articleSummary: 2026-07-16: National CDC press briefing on science-based heat relief and disease prevention reports mainland COVID-19 remains intermittently at low transmission since October 2025, with a recent uptick in positivity but overall low; dominant lineage NB.1.8.1, no new variants of public health concern detected. China CDC spokesperson Xi Jingjing warns summer conditions boost vector activity and population movement, elevating risks of dengue fever and chikungunya fever in southern provinces and potential local outbreaks from imported cases. Respiratory illnesses stay low, with rhinovirus and parainfluenza activity noted. Flood-season threats could impair sanitation and water safety, increasing diarrheal, respiratory, and vector-borne disease risks. Prevention centers on four pillars: legal enforcement, joint prevention, policy improvements, and patriotic health campaigns. Since 2026-04-01, chikungunya is Category B infectious disease, enabling surveillance, emergency response, medical treatment, and enhanced border screening with customs and immigration.

article.articleHeadline: El ébola mantiene una intensa transmisión en RDC: 2.073 casos y 796 fallecimientos confirmados
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola maintains intense transmission in the DRC: 2,073 cases and 796 confirmed deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues with 2,073 confirmed cases and 796 deaths since May 15, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus. The outbreak spans five provinces—Ituri, North Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, and South Kivu—across 45 health zones, amid insecurity, population displacement, and cross-border movement with Uganda and South Sudan. Ituri remains the epicenter, accounting for about 90% of cases (1,863) and 668 deaths; North Kivu has 189 cases and 111 deaths (case fatality 58.7%). Haut-Uélé has 14 cases and 13 deaths; Tshopo 4 cases. In the last 24 hours, 62 new confirmed cases and 42 deaths were reported. Healthcare workers total 119 infections, 36 deaths. Response includes 737 patients in isolation, 12,000+ contacts followed (76.6%), and new treatment centers (Kasenyi, 80 beds; Bambu, 50 beds). Challenges include community resistance, ambulance and diagnostic shortages, funding gaps, and insecurity.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱、コンゴ民主共和国で激しい感染拡大続く:2,073症例、796人の死亡が確認

triage.notes: ウガンダ・南スーダンとの国境地域での人口移動があり越境拡大リスクがあるが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。
